statement: The supplied sources contain no derivation (including via polynomial root finding); pole location is defined as follows: for a function f meromorphic in an open domain U, a point z_0 is a pole of f if it is a zero of 1/f and 1/f is holomorphic in some neighbourhood of z_0. Equivalently, there exists an integer n > 0 such that (z - z_0)^n f(z) is holomorphic and nonzero in a neighbourhood of z_0, where n is the order (or multiplicity) of the pole at z_0.

symbols.meaning: complex-valued function of a complex variable
location of the pole in the complex plane
open domain in the complex plane
coefficients of the Laurent series expansion

properties.property: A pole of f is a zero of 1/f, and a zero of f is a pole of 1/f.
properties.why: Follows from the definition of a pole as a zero of 1/f where 1/f is holomorphic.

properties.property: Poles of a meromorphic function are isolated.
properties.why: Follows because (z - z_0)^n f(z) is holomorphic and nonzero in a neighbourhood of z_0.

properties.property: In a neighbourhood of a pole z_0 of order n, f(z) has a Laurent series with at most finite principal part of n terms: f(z) = \sum_{k \geq -n} a_k (z - z_0)^k with a_{-n} \neq 0.
properties.why: Follows from the analyticity of (z - z_0)^n f(z) in a neighbourhood of z_0.

properties.property: On the whole Riemann sphere, the sum of the orders of the poles of a meromorphic function equals the sum of the orders of its zeros.
properties.why: Follows from extending meromorphic functions to the Riemann sphere with zeros and poles at infinity.

properties.property: For every rational function on the whole Riemann sphere, the sum of orders of its poles is the maximum of the degrees of its numerator and denominator.
properties.why: Follows from rational functions being meromorphic on the whole Riemann sphere.

assumptions.assumption: f is meromorphic in an open neighbourhood of z_0.
assumptions.breaks_when: f fails to be complex differentiable or at least one of f and 1/f fails to be holomorphic in a neighbourhood of each point.

assumptions.assumption: The singularity at z_0 is of finite order (non-removable but not essential).
assumptions.breaks_when: z_0 is an essential singularity, where no integer n exists such that (z - z_0)^n f(z) is holomorphic and nonzero near z_0.

failure_modes.signature: The Laurent series around z_0 has infinitely many negative-power terms, and no integer n makes (z - z_0)^n f(z) holomorphic and nonzero.
failure_modes.cause: z_0 is an essential singularity rather than a pole.

failure_modes.signature: Every neighbourhood of z_0 contains other singularities or zeros.
failure_modes.cause: Poles must be isolated; non-isolated singular behavior violates the definition of a meromorphic function.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so pole_location is recorded as a definition
